--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: fff680
+title: 'kanban CLI: --tags joins an array into one hyphen-joined tag'
+---
+The `kanban` CLI does not split a `--tags` array. It joins the whole argument
+into one tag name. This is the same defect class as ^4nzhg4s, on the CLI
+surface instead of the MCP dispatch surface.
+
+## What happens
+
+Measured on a fresh board, with a binary built at `c157c8a72`:
+
+```
+kanban task add    --title T1 --description hello --tags '["red","blue"]'
+kanban task update --id <id> --tags '["red","blue"]'
+kanban task tag    --id <id> --tags '["beta","gamma"]'
+```
+
+Each call reports `ok: true`. Each writes ONE tag:
+
+```
+hello #red-blue
+hi #red-blue
+hello #alpha #beta-gamma
+```
+
+The caller asked for two tags and got one. A scalar (`--tags 'alpha'`) is
+correct, so only the array shape is affected.
+
+## Where it is NOT
+
+`dispatch::ref_list` is correct. It parses a stringified JSON array back into
+its elements, and `tag_refs` / `req_tag_refs` route `tags` and `tag` through
+it. ^4nzhg4s fixed that path and its tests pass. So the CLI either does not
+reach `ref_list` for this param, or it mangles the value before dispatch.
+Start at the `kanban-cli` argument layer for `--tags`.
+
+## Blast radius
+
+All three writing ops take `--tags`: `task add`, `task update`, `task tag`.
+`untag` takes the same param and is very likely affected too. Every joined
+name also mints a tag entity nobody asked for, so each call leaves debris on
+the board — the same debris ^4nzhg4s had to sweep.
+
+Found while sweeping the board for ^4nzhg4s: a CLI `--tags` call made during
+that sweep created the tag `code-context-indexer` on the live board. The card
+body and the stray entity were both reverted.
+
+## Work
+
+- Route the CLI `--tags` param through the same shape normalizer the dispatch
+  layer uses, so an array, a scalar, and a stringified array each mean one tag
+  for each element.
+- Check `--assignees`, `--depends_on`, and `--attachments` on the CLI for the
+  same gap; they share the forgiving-list contract.
+- Add a CLI-level test that passes two tags in one call and asserts two tags on
+  the task. A dispatch-level test does not cover this — the defect lives above
+  dispatch.
+
+## Done when
+
+One CLI call applies two separate tags, and no CLI call mints a hyphen-joined
+name the caller did not ask for. #bug #kanban #cli
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m14kcrbms180kryrr637jkfz
+  text: |-
+    Research done. Reproduced RED with a binary built at HEAD (158012bcc) against a temp board in the scratchpad: `kanban task add --title T1 --description hello --tags '["red","blue"]'` writes ONE tag `red-blue`.
+
+    Root cause, above dispatch: the CLI arg tree is generated by the shared engine `crates/swissarmyhammer-operations/src/cli_gen.rs`. A schema property typed `array` becomes a clap `ArgAction::Append` arg, and `extract_value_from_matches` turns each occurrence into ONE JSON string element. So one `--tags '["red","blue"]'` reaches dispatch as `["[\"red\",\"blue\"]"]` — an array holding ONE stringified array. `dispatch::ref_list` expands a stringified array only when the WHOLE value is a string, so the element stays whole and the tag sanitizer joins it to `red-blue`.
+
+    Which params share the gap (measured from `--help` value names and the op structs):
+    - `--tags` (`Vec<String>`) — array — BROKEN on add/update/tag/untag.
+    - `--assignees` (`Vec<ActorId>`) — array — BROKEN. `--assignees '["alice","bob"]'` exits 1 with no message at all.
+    - `--depends_on` (`Vec<TaskId>`) — array — BROKEN.
+    - `--attachments` (`Option<Value>` on update task) — typed as a plain string, so the whole value reaches `ref_list` and already expands correctly. Covered by a test to keep it that way.
+
+    Fix shape: one shared normalizer in `swissarmyhammer-operations`, used by BOTH `cli_gen`'s array extraction and `dispatch::ref_list`'s string branch, so a stringified array means one entry for each element on every surface. The fix lands in the shared engine, so every op CLI (kanban, sah, code-context, shelltool) gets it.

+    Implementation landed, TDD RED to GREEN.
+
+    RED, before the change:
+    - `cargo nextest run -p swissarmyhammer-operations cli_gen` — 2 of the 3 new generator tests failed. The failure printed `["alice", "[\"bob\",\"carol\"]"]` where the test asked for `["alice","bob","carol"]`.

+    The change:
+    - New `crates/swissarmyhammer-operations/src/forgiving.rs` — `expand_list_entry(raw)`, the one reading of a list value: a string that parses as a JSON array of strings expands to those strings, every other string is one entry kept whole.

+    - `dispatch::ref_list` calls the same function for its string branch, so the CLI and MCP surfaces cannot drift apart.
